clue.text: Pure heroin, the very least part ecstasy

blocks.note: snow is slang for a powdered drug such as heroin or cocaine
a whit is the smallest possible amount
E is the usual abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug dealer boasts that the heroin is uncut, with barely a trace of ecstasy in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow-white describes something spotless and untainted, a figurative synonym for pure.

clue.text: Office hours held by canoness

indicators.note: what is held by a word sits inside it, so the answer lies within the next word

blocks.note: the letters run unbroken inside this word

explanation.surface: A nun is keeping set hours of work, like an office clerk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office' is the church sense: the daily round of services. A canoness is a woman living under a religious rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Nones is the monastic service said at the ninth hour of daylight, one of the canonical hours of the divine office.

clue.text: Historically, underwear used to be a desirable luxury

blocks.note: past tense of to be
pie in the slangy sense of a treat or something pleasant to have, as in pie in the sky

explanation.surface: Fancy underwear was once a coveted luxury, a fashion-history remark.
explanation.walkthrough: A waspie is a corset that cinched the waist into a wasp shape, popular in the 1950s, hence 'Historically'.
explanation.definitionFit: A waspie is a short corset worn to narrow the waist, a dated item of women's lingerie.

clue.text: Capital artist stops race

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so one word sits inside the other like a cork

blocks.note: to hare is to run very fast
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A painter halts a running contest, perhaps by walking onto the track.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the standard crossword artist; 'race' is a verb here, to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Harare is the capital city of Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Destroy ring, essentially beating raised gemstone

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letter is kept
in a down clue, raising the letters makes them read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to zap is to wipe out
O is ring-shaped
the middle letter of this seven-letter word

explanation.surface: Someone smashes a ring, beating out its precious stone in a fantasy quest.
explanation.definitionFit: Topaz is a precious mineral, usually yellow, cut and set as a gem.

clue.text: Greeting content changed by a third

indicators.note: something changed is altered, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: content means pleased or satisfied
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A message whose content has been altered by a third party.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy birthday is the standard salutation offered on someone's anniversary of birth.

clue.text: For example, OAP cronies upset with general computing and international religion

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the word before is rearranged

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
IT, information technology, is computing in general
I is the abbreviation for international
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A pensioner's pals are bothered by computers and global spirituality.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP stands for old-age pensioner, the British term for someone drawing a state pension.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-age pensioner is an instance of an elderly person, which the phrase names, hence 'For example'.

clue.text: Means to uncover what Toulouse-Lautrec may have done?

blocks.note: first meaning: a chemical that removes old coats of paint from a surface
second meaning, read as two words: the artist could paint a woman who strips

explanation.walkthrough: Toulouse-Lautrec painted the dancers and cabaret women of Montmartre, so the phrase splits into a verb and its subject matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The solvent lifts paint off wood or metal, revealing the bare surface below, while the split reading is an artist's choice of model.

clue.text: Mark following note penned by north African dignitary

indicators.note: one piece coming after the other fixes the order in which they are joined
something penned is shut in an enclosure, so these letters go inside another word

blocks.note: the Moors were a people of north-west Africa
n. is the abbreviation for a note, as in a footnote reference
a sign is a mark or symbol

explanation.surface: A North African official signs a document after a note is written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the mark after the note, and that pair then sits inside the African's name after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Monsignor is the honorary title of a senior Roman Catholic prelate, a church dignitary.

clue.text: Vendor's state-of-the-art herb garden perfect at the end

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: only the endings of the two words are wanted, the final letter of each

blocks.note: the latest thing is new
sage is a culinary herb
the last letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A seller boasts that the modern herb garden looks perfect at the end of the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsagent is a shopkeeper who sells newspapers and magazines, a kind of vendor.

clue.text: Almost resist mates

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: to oppose is to resist

explanation.surface: Someone nearly fights back against their friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Oppos is British slang, originally naval, for pals.
explanation.definitionFit: An oppo is an informal British word for a close friend or colleague, from 'opposite number'.

clue.text: Former republic's unknown northern river

blocks.note: algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns
the Aire is a river in Yorkshire in the north of England

explanation.surface: An old state has a river in its north that nobody has mapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Zaire was the name of the Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1971 to 1997.

clue.text: Move back in compact valleys

indicators.note: the instruction moves a word's back, its final letter, inward, reordering it

blocks.note: dense means closely packed

explanation.surface: An instruction to return to tightly packed valleys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move back' reads as return; here 'back' is the word's last letter, which moves one place in.
explanation.definitionFit: A dene, or dean, is a narrow wooded valley, a word found in English place names.

clue.text: Light up welcome message in city

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from the bottom upward

blocks.note: an LED is a light-emitting diode
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A sign lights up with a welcome as you arrive in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi is the major Indian city containing the capital, New Delhi.

clue.text: Decamp, not quite going over one's first scar?

indicators.note: not quite whole means the word is cut short by its last letter
going over suggests turning over, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to levant is an old British slang verb for running off, especially to dodge debts

explanation.surface: Someone running away has nearly fallen over and picked up a first scar.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the belly button is the mark left by the cut umbilical cord, the first scar anyone has.
explanation.definitionFit: The navel marks where the umbilical cord was severed at birth, so it is jokingly the earliest scar of a life.

clue.text: Cheeky goat making every possible volte-face?

blocks.clueFragment: Cheeky goat making every possible volte-face?
blocks.note: surface reading: an impudent goat turning this way and that at every chance
setter's reading: a goat word that reverses direction at each opportunity

explanation.surface: An impudent goat keeps doing U-turns wherever it can.
explanation.walkthrough: The published hint says a female goat goes in the opposite direction at each opportunity, three times; the full letter-by-letter parse is uncertain, so treat 'Cheeky' as the sure route in.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassy is an informal, chiefly American word for impertinent or lively in a bold way.

clue.text: Overcome unpaid loan?

blocks.note: a sub is an advance on wages
money still owed is due

explanation.surface: A borrower is defeated by a loan that has not been paid back.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is read in reverse clue order: the loan comes first, then the unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: To subdue is to conquer or bring under control, a synonym of the verb overcome.

clue.text: Article covering my small fruits

indicators.note: a cover goes around something, so the article's letters wrap the next word

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece covering the writer's tiny fruit crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' looks like a possessive but is an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Acorns are the nuts of the oak, which botanically count as fruits.

clue.text: Dropping name, whine about jeans

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away, so a letter is removed
about can mean turned around, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name, the letter dropped
to snivel is to whine tearfully

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to name names and complains about their jeans.
explanation.definitionFit: Levi's is the brand name of the original denim jeans, used for jeans generally.

clue.text: Bale perhaps last from pile in local yard

indicators.note: the last from a word is its final letter alone
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a garth is a dialect word, chiefly northern English, for a yard or enclosure
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A farmer leaves the last hay bale from the stack in the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bale' is not hay but the Welsh footballer Gareth Bale, so 'perhaps' marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Gareth is the first name of Gareth Bale, the Welsh footballer, so it is one possible Bale forename.

clue.text: Jump, turning right into middle of royal's furtive activity?

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter only
turning into something means changing into it, so one letter is swapped for another

blocks.note: to spring is to jump
R is the abbreviation for right, the letter replaced
the central letter of this five-letter word

explanation.surface: A royal sneakily leaps aside at the halfway point, a palace intrigue.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying is the secret gathering of information, a stealthy activity, hence the question mark for a loose definition.

clue.text: Whisky arguably ain't associated with the clergy?

blocks.note: ain't is a nonstandard form of isn't, so 'arguably' asks us to read it as a form of the verb 'is'
lay people are not ordained, so this reading is the opposite; the question mark flags the twist

explanation.surface: Someone claims whisky has nothing to do with churchmen.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces together read as a statement that something is not clerical; 'arguably' concedes that ain't is only loosely a form of 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Islay is a Hebridean island whose distilleries produce peaty single malt Scotch, so the island's name stands for its whisky.

clue.text: Raise foot support that's run loose?

indicators.note: a run let loose escapes, so the abbreviation for run is removed from the word

blocks.note: a stirrup holds a rider's foot
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A rider lifts a footrest that has worked loose.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up is to provoke or arouse, as in raising trouble or a commotion.

clue.text: Temporary shelter maybe showing fatigue when tipped

indicators.note: tipping a word cuts off its tip, its first letter

blocks.note: yawning is a sign of tiredness

explanation.surface: A makeshift tent shows signs of tiredness as it tips over.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canvas sheet stretched out to give shade or cover, a kind of provisional shelter.

clue.text: Mineral chart enters pigment

indicators.note: entering something means going inside it

blocks.note: ore is a mineral-bearing rock
ch. is an abbreviation for chart

explanation.surface: A mineral chart is included in a guide to paint colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown clay used as a natural colouring.

clue.text: Exotic, eschewing new system of morals

indicators.note: eschewing means avoiding, so the word goes without the abbreviation for new

blocks.note: ethnic in the loose sense of foreign or exotic
N is the abbreviation for new, the letter removed

explanation.surface: An unusual moral code that rejects anything new.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a set of moral principles, such as the work ethic.

clue.text: Shoot extremely sadistic overthrown chief

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, first and last letters
something overthrown is turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the first and last letters of this word
the chief is number one, written NO 1, with the 1 as I

explanation.surface: A cruel leader is toppled and shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A scion is a young shoot or twig cut for grafting, the botanical sense of the word.

clue.text: Bomber Harris ultimately supported by those who volunteered to protect their country

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is used
to protect is to surround and guard, so one piece wraps another
in a down clue, something supported sits on top of what holds it up

blocks.note: the final letter of this name
the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
the country the Territorials defend

explanation.surface: Wartime RAF chief 'Bomber' Harris was backed by volunteers defending Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur 'Bomber' Harris led RAF Bomber Command, so the name looks like the definition; the bomber is a German one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stuka was the Junkers Ju 87, a German dive bomber of the Second World War.

clue.text: Experienced older men loaded USAF freighter

indicators.note: loaded can mean drunk, and a drunk's letters are scrambled

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Veteran airmen are packed aboard an American air force cargo plane.
explanation.walkthrough: USAF is the United States Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Father figures are older men whose experience makes them mentors or role models.

clue.text: Patsy's son caught two animals

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an ape and a goat

explanation.surface: Patsy's boy has trapped a pair of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Patsy looks like a woman's name; here it is a dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: A patsy is a person who takes the blame for others, the same role as a fall guy.
